clinician.final_diagnosis: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome Associated with Varicella-Zoster Virus Encephalitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 8-year-old previously healthy boy with up-to-date varicella vaccination presented with a 3-day history of fever, progressive left ear pain and swelling, and vesicular rash around the left ear pinna. On admission day 2, he developed lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy component of Ramsay Hunt Syndrome). On admission day 3, he developed vomiting, dysarthria, and unsteady gait—neurological manifestations consistent with encephalitis. Brain MRI and MRV performed on day 3 were normal. IV acyclovir (15 mg/kg/dose 8 hourly) and prednisolone (1 mg/kg daily) were initiated on day 3 of admission. Over the following days, his ear pain, swelling, vomiting, and gait disturbance improved significantly. He was asymptomatic at discharge after 10 days of IV acyclovir and 7 days of prednisolone, with supportive eye care and physiotherapy. At 6-month follow-up, he remained completely asymptomatic with normal MRI and no evidence of cerebral arteritis or vasculopathies.
